attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

meta:
  venue: EMNLP 2026
  track: findings
  submission_system: ARR June 2026 cycle
  template: templates/latex/acl2023/
  template_note: "标准 ACL LaTeX 模板 (acl2023.sty)，ARR/ACL/EMNLP 2026 通用"
  page_limit: 8
  deadline: 2026-06-15
  title: "Aggregate Convergence, Per-Example Divergence: Decoupled Effects of Attention in Hybrid Recurrent Architectures"
  core_claim: >
    Adding attention to hybrid recurrent architectures (GDN, RetNet, HGRN2) reduces
    cross-architecture variance by 79% on LAMBADA (BCa CI [-1.0, -0.7]), but per-example
    helped/hurt sets remain nearly disjoint (Jaccard < 0.10) and saturate at minimal
    attention — aggregate convergence and per-example divergence are decoupled,
    quantifying underspecification in hybrid architecture design.
  created_at: 2026-05-19T18:00:00Z

  # D009 统计硬约束
  statistical_constraints:
    primary_evidence: "BCa percentile CI [-1.0, -0.7] (valid-only, 88.75%)"
    permutation_test: "exact, two-tailed, n=5, 120 permutations"
    bonferroni: "6-benchmark pre-registered adj-p=0.100; report 'does not survive strict Bonferroni'"
    prohibited:
      - "post-hoc subset Bonferroni (e.g. '2-benchmark Bonferroni', 'only rho<0 benchmarks')"
      - "'mechanistic analysis' → use 'characterization' / 'decomposition'"
      - "'paradox' / 'paradoxical' / 'co-evolution' / 'co-evolve'"
      - "'significantly improves' without statistical test"
      - "'state-of-the-art' (no SOTA comparison)"
      - "'consistently outperforms' (1 benchmark only)"

  # 叙事约束
  narrative_constraints:
    prohibited_terms:
      - paradox
      - paradoxical
      - co-evolution
      - co-evolve
      - paradoxical coexistence
      - mechanistic analysis
      - remarkably
      - extensive experiments demonstrate
    replacement_map:
      co-evolution: "decoupling"
      paradox: "divergence"
      mechanistic analysis: "characterization"
    honest_reporting:
      - "Bonferroni adj-p=0.100 does not survive strict correction"
      - "BCa degenerate resamples (11.25%) excluded; formal justification in appendix"
      - "n=5 attention ratios limits statistical power (min p≈0.008)"
      - "Per-example analysis limited to LAMBADA only"
      - "Two scale points (340M, 1.3B) — binary contrast, not trend"

# ============================================================
#  PAPER OUTLINE
# ============================================================
paper_outline:
  - section: abstract
    word_budget: 200
    core_bullets:
      - "Context: hybrid recurrent architectures (linear recurrence + attention) increasingly standard, but per-example behavioral effects of attention poorly quantified"
      - "Method: systematic analysis using Wang et al.'s model zoo — 3 architectures × 5 attention ratios × 2 scales, 10 benchmarks, 5153 per-example comparisons"
      - "C1: across 10 benchmarks, significant convergence only on LAMBADA (rho=-1.0, BCa CI [-1.0,-0.7], cross-arch std drops 79%)"
      - "C3: despite aggregate convergence, per-example helped/hurt sets nearly disjoint (Jaccard < 0.10) — decoupled from aggregate trend, saturating at minimal (4%) attention"
      - "C2: convergence complete at 1.3B but partial/non-monotonic at 340M"
      - "Implication: quantifies underspecification in hybrid architecture design"
    dependencies: [experiments, method, introduction]
    registry_refs: [exp-001, exp-008, exp-010, exp-011]

  - section: introduction
    word_budget: 1000
    core_bullets:
      - "Hook: adding attention to three different recurrent architectures makes LAMBADA performance near-identical (std 0.024→0.005), yet they achieve this by helping/hurting almost entirely different examples (Jaccard < 0.10)"
      - "Context: hybrid recurrent-attention architectures (Jamba, Griffin, RWKV-6) mainstream; Wang et al. (2025) provide 72-model zoo — but no per-example analysis"
      - "Gap: aggregate benchmark comparisons mask per-example behavioral diversity; this gap is well-documented (D'Amour et al. 2022) but unquantified for hybrid architectures"
      - "Our contribution: first systematic per-example analysis; three findings — (1) task-specific convergence, (2) scale-dependent convergence, (3) per-example divergence decoupled from aggregate convergence"
      - "Insight preview: aggregate σ decreases gradually across 5 attention levels; Jaccard saturates at first level (4%) — different timescales = decoupling"
      - "Paper structure and Figure 1 forward reference"
    dependencies: [experiments]
    figures: [fig1_decoupling_hero]
    citation_hints:
      - "Wang et al. (2025) model zoo — primary data source"
      - "D'Amour et al. (2022) underspecification — framing anchor"
      - "Jamba (Lieber et al. 2024), Griffin (De et al. 2024) — hybrid arch motivation"
    registry_refs: [exp-001, exp-010]

  - section: related_work
    word_budget: 750
    core_bullets:
      - "§ Hybrid recurrent architectures: Jamba, RWKV-6, Griffin/RecurrentGemma, Mamba-2 → we analyze these designs, not propose new ones"
      - "§ Linear recurrent models: S4, Mamba, RetNet, HGRN2, GatedDeltaNet → the base architectures in our study"
      - "§ Underspecification + model agreement: D'Amour et al. 2022, Fort et al. 2019, McCoy et al. 2020 → our finding is a specific instance; we quantify, not discover"
      - "§ Ensemble diversity: Krogh & Vedelsby 1995, Kuncheva & Whitaker 2003 → per-example divergence expected in diverse ensembles; hybrid models are not ensembles but exhibit similar patterns"
      - "§ Dataset cartography + per-example analysis: Swayamdipta et al. 2020, IRT (Rodriguez et al. 2021) → per-example difficulty modeling"
      - "§ Attention analysis: Clark et al. 2019, Jain & Wallace 2019, Olsson et al. 2022 → descriptive attention analysis background"
      - "Positioning: we do NOT claim discovery of per-example divergence; contribution is quantifying it in hybrid architectures with controlled attention variation"
    dependencies: [introduction]
    citation_hints:
      - "Must-cite: D'Amour et al. 2022, Wang et al. 2025, Krogh & Vedelsby 1995, Swayamdipta et al. 2020"
      - "Must-engage: Jamba, Mamba, Griffin"
      - "CKA (Kornblith et al. 2019) — representation similarity context"

  - section: method
    word_budget: 750
    core_bullets:
      - "§3.1 Model Zoo: Wang et al. (2025) pretrained — 3 architectures (GatedDeltaNet, RetNet, HGRN2) × 5 attention ratios (0%, 4%, 7.7%, 14.3%, 25%) × 2 scales (340M, 1.3B); pure = 0% attention; h-k-1 = 1 attention layer per k+1 layers; transformer baseline"
      - "§3.2 Task Taxonomy (pre-defined, D003, NOT post-hoc): pure context retrieval = next-token prediction requiring long-range context without reasoning/knowledge (LAMBADA); comprehension = reading comprehension/QA (BoolQ); reasoning = commonsense/inference (HellaSwag, ARC-C, WinoGrande, PIQA, COPA); mixed = multiple skills (ARC-E, MMLU, SciQ, xstorycloze_en)"
      - "§3.3 Convergence Metrics: cross-arch std σ across 3 architectures at each attention ratio; Spearman ρ between attention ratio rank and σ; convergence ratio = σ_pure / σ_{h3-1}"
      - "§3.4 Per-Example Decomposition: helped = acc_hybrid > acc_pure; hurt = acc_hybrid < acc_pure; net effect = helped - hurt; pairwise Jaccard J = |A∩B| / |A∪B| across architecture pairs"
      - "§3.5 Statistical Methods: exact permutation test (n=5, 120 perms, two-tailed); BCa bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, architecture-level); Bonferroni correction (6 benchmarks pre-registered D003); Mann-Whitney U for within-arch comparisons; Kruskal-Wallis for cross-arch comparisons"
    dependencies: []
    notation_table:
      σ: "cross-architecture standard deviation"
      ρ: "Spearman rank correlation"
      J: "pairwise Jaccard similarity"
      h-k-1: "hybrid with 1 attention layer per k+1 total layers (e.g., h3-1 = 25% attention)"
    registry_refs: [exp-001, exp-008]

  - section: experiments
    word_budget: 1800
    core_bullets:
      - "§4.1 Task-Specific Convergence (C1): Table 1 shows 10 benchmarks; only LAMBADA has ρ=-1.0 (p=0.017 exact perm); BCa CI [-1.0, -0.7]; σ drops 0.024→0.005 (79%); Bonferroni adj-p=0.100 'does not survive strict correction'; task-specificity IS the finding — LAMBADA uniquely tests pure context retrieval; Figure 2 forest plot visualizes"
      - "§4.2 Scale-Dependent Convergence (C2): 1.3B monotonically converges (ρ=-1.0); 340M partial convergence (56% σ reduction but non-monotonic rebound at h3-1); binary contrast — scale is necessary condition for complete equalization; two data points, NOT a scalable trend"
      - "§4.3 Per-Example Divergence (C3a): Table 2 — pairwise Jaccard < 0.10 for all architecture pairs; GDN net -153, HGRN2 net +153, RetNet net -69; surface features do NOT differentiate helped/hurt within arch (exp-003 negative); BUT cross-arch Kruskal-Wallis p=0.0005 for hurt samples → architecture-specificity is structured, not random"
      - "§4.4 Decoupling (C3b, title-level contribution): Figure 1 — aggregate σ decreases gradually (0.024→0.016→0.014→0.006→0.005) across 5 attention levels; Jaccard saturates at first level (4%→~0.095) and stays flat; net asymmetry increases (0.013→0.040); aggregate convergence and per-example divergence operate on different timescales = decoupling. Attention weight analysis (exp-004-r2): GDN↔RetNet L2 cosine=0.995 yet per-example effects differ → divergence not in attention layer but in recurrent layers; HGRN2↔others cosine~0.20 in early layers, converges >0.94 at L20. 1-2 sentences in text, full 8-layer × 3-pair data in Appendix D."
      - "§4.5 Robustness (brief, details in appendix): GDN-excluded sensitivity — LAMBADA ρ→-0.7 (p=0.233), MMLU flips +0.6 (D007); BCa degenerate resamples 11.25% formally justified"
    dependencies: [method]
    tables: [tab1_convergence, tab2_per_example]
    figures: [fig2_task_specificity]
    registry_refs: [exp-001, exp-003, exp-003-p2, exp-004-r2, exp-008, exp-009, exp-010, exp-011, exp-011-xstorycloze, eval_340m_retnet_hgrn2]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 350
    core_bullets:
      - "Summary: first systematic per-example analysis of attention's equalizing effect in hybrid recurrent architectures — decoupling is title-level contribution"
      - "Key findings recap: (1) task-specific convergence on LAMBADA only, (2) scale-dependent (1.3B complete, 340M partial), (3) aggregate convergence and per-example divergence decoupled"
      - "Practical implication: architecture selection based on aggregate benchmarks may mask per-example behavioral differences that matter for deployment"
      - "Future work: interventional experiments (attention head ablation/swaps); scaling beyond 1.3B; other hybrid families (Jamba, RWKV-6); fine-tuning analysis"
    dependencies: [experiments]
    registry_refs: [exp-001, exp-010]

  - section: limitations
    word_budget: 300
    core_bullets:
      - "n=5 attention ratios: minimum achievable p≈0.008, statistical power inherently limited"
      - "LAMBADA-only per-example analysis: sample-level decomposition requires significant convergence benchmark"
      - "Two scale points (340M, 1.3B): binary contrast, not scalable trend; 7B+ unavailable"
      - "Three architectures (GDN, RetNet, HGRN2): more families needed to generalize"
      - "Descriptive, not causal: attention weight analysis is observational; interventional experiments = future work"
      - "Pre-trained only: no fine-tuning or downstream task adaptation analysis"
    dependencies: [experiments]

    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: "Hero figure: 2-panel showing decoupling of aggregate convergence and per-example divergence"

      Aggregate convergence (cross-arch std drops 79%) and per-example divergence

      - "Panel (b) 'Per-Example Divergence': scatter+line of Jaccard vs attention ratio; separate markers for J(helped) and J(hurt); flat reference band (axhspan) at ~0.09-0.10 to emphasize saturation; x starts at 4% (no pure data); annotate 'saturates at 4%'"

1	---
2	name: paper-writing-norms
3	description: 顶会级别论文写作风格规范——章节写法（Abstract/Intro/Related Work）、去 AI 风格、视觉密度、叙事哲学。Paper Agent 和 Worker 写论文章节时必须加载。
4	allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep]
5	scope: global
6	version: 2
7	priority: 9
8	tags:
9	  - writing
10	  - paper
11	  - style
12	  - norms
13	roles:
14	  - agent
15	  - worker
16	  - paper_agent
17	---
18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

1	\section{Experiments}\label{sec:experiments}
2	
3	We analyze how attention affects cross-architecture performance variance using models from the hybrid recurrent model zoo of \citet{wang2025hybrid}. Our analysis spans three architectures (GatedDeltaNet, RetNet, HGRN2), five attention ratios (0\% pure recurrent, 4\%, 7.7\%, 14.3\%, 25\%), and two scales (340M and 1.3B parameters). In the h$k$-1 notation used throughout, one attention layer is interleaved per every $k{+}1$ layers; h3-1 denotes 25\% attention. All models within each scale share identical training data and hyperparameters; they differ only in architecture and attention configuration. We evaluate on 10 benchmarks spanning retrieval, comprehension, reasoning, and mixed task categories, plus one supplementary benchmark (COPA, $n = 100$).
4	
5	\subsection{Task-Specific Convergence}\label{ssec:task_convergence}
6	
7	We first ask whether adding attention layers reduces performance differences between architectures, and whether any such reduction is uniform across tasks. For each benchmark, we compute the cross-architecture standard deviation ($\sigma$) at each attention ratio and measure the Spearman rank correlation ($\rho$) between attention ratio and $\sigma$ across the five configurations.
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:convergence} reports results for all benchmarks at 1.3B scale. LAMBADA is the only benchmark exhibiting monotonic convergence: $\rho = -1.0$ (exact permutation test, $p = .017$, two-tailed, $n = 5$, 120 permutations). Cross-architecture $\sigma$ drops from 0.024 to 0.005, a 79\% reduction. The 95\% BCa percentile bootstrap confidence interval for $\rho$ is $[-1.0, -0.7]$ (10{,}000 resamples), which excludes zero. After Bonferroni correction for six pre-registered benchmarks, the adjusted $p = .100$ does not survive strict Bonferroni correction at $\alpha = 0.05$. We therefore treat the confidence interval, rather than the corrected $p$-value, as the primary evidence for the LAMBADA convergence effect.
10	
11	The task-specificity of this result is itself a finding. LAMBADA \citep{paperno2016lambada} is a pure context retrieval task: predicting the final word of a passage requires encoding long-range dependencies but no multi-step reasoning. Attention provides direct token-level access to the full context, so convergence on a retrieval task is consistent with attention compensating for differences in how recurrent architectures store and recall contextual information. The remaining benchmarks span comprehension (BoolQ), reasoning (HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, WinoGrande, PIQA), and mixed demands (ARC-Easy, MMLU, SciQ, XStoryCloze). None shows significant convergence: all have $|\rho| \leq 0.7$ and $p \geq .233$. Two mixed benchmarks (ARC-Easy, MMLU) exhibit moderate negative correlations ($\rho = -0.7$) and high convergence ratios (7.70 and 2.27, respectively), but their non-monotonic trajectories prevent these correlations from reaching significance. The supplementary benchmark COPA shows a similar convergence ratio (5.57, $\rho = -0.67$) but is limited by its small sample size. For tasks that involve reasoning or comprehension beyond retrieval, architectural differences in recurrent layers remain performance-relevant regardless of attention allocation (Figure~\ref{fig:task_specificity}).
12	
13	\begin{figure}[t]
14	\centering
15	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig2_task_specificity.pdf}
16	\caption{Spearman $\rho$ between attention ratio and cross-architecture $\sigma$ for each benchmark at 1.3B scale. LAMBADA ($\rho = -1.0$; BCa 95\% CI $[-1.0, -0.7]$) is the only benchmark with a negative correlation whose confidence interval excludes zero. Benchmarks are grouped by task category.}
17	\label{fig:task_specificity}
18	\end{figure}
19	
20	\begin{table*}[t]
21	\centering
22	\caption{Cross-architecture convergence across benchmarks (1.3B scale). $\rho$: Spearman correlation between attention ratio and cross-architecture $\sigma$ across five configurations. $p$: exact permutation test (two-tailed, 120 permutations). $\sigma$ values reported $\times 10^{2}$ (accuracy percentage points). Ratio: $\sigma_{\text{pure}} / \sigma_{\text{h3-1}}$. \textbf{Bold}: only benchmark with $\rho = -1.0$.}
23	\label{tab:convergence}
24	\begin{tabular}{llrrrrr}
25	\toprule
26	Benchmark & Category & $\rho$ & $p$ & $\sigma_{\text{pure}}$ & $\sigma_{\text{h3-1}}$ & Ratio \\
27	\midrule

29	BoolQ & Comprehension & $0.2$ & .783 & 1.63 & 2.36 & 0.69 \\
30	ARC-C & Reasoning & $0.6$ & .350 & 0.96 & 1.32 & 0.72 \\
31	HellaSwag & Reasoning & $0.3$ & .683 & 1.17 & 1.18 & 0.99 \\
32	PIQA & Reasoning & $-0.5$ & .450 & 0.54 & 0.34 & 1.59 \\
33	WinoGrande & Reasoning & $0.1$ & .950 & 0.67 & 0.78 & 0.86 \\
34	ARC-E & Mixed & $-0.7$ & .233 & 1.00 & 0.13 & 7.70 \\
35	MMLU & Mixed & $-0.7$ & .233 & 0.92 & 0.41 & 2.27 \\
36	SciQ & Mixed & $0.1$ & .950 & 0.87 & 0.74 & 1.19 \\
37	XStoryCloze & Mixed & $-0.6$ & .350 & 0.82 & 0.55 & 1.49 \\
38	\midrule
39	COPA$^{\dagger}$ & Reasoning & $-0.67$ & .267 & 2.63 & 0.47 & 5.57 \\
40	\bottomrule
41	\multicolumn{7}{l}{\footnotesize $^{\dagger}$Supplementary ($n = 100$); excluded from multiple comparison correction.}
42	\end{tabular}
43	\end{table*}
44	
45	\subsection{Scale-Dependent Convergence}\label{ssec:scale_convergence}
46	
47	We compare the LAMBADA convergence pattern at two scales. At 1.3B parameters, convergence is monotonic: $\sigma$ decreases at every attention level from 0\% through 25\% ($\rho = -1.0$). At 340M, convergence is partial. $\sigma$ reaches a maximum reduction of 56\% at intermediate attention ratios, but rebounds at h3-1, yielding a net endpoint reduction of 39\%: the trajectory is non-monotonic, and the highest-attention model does not achieve the lowest cross-architecture variance. One possible interpretation is that at smaller scale, the capacity overhead of attention layers creates interference that offsets the retrieval benefit.
48	
49	This contrast indicates that sufficient scale is a necessary condition for complete equalization on LAMBADA. We emphasize that this is a binary observation from two data points, not a scaling law. Characterizing the functional relationship between scale and convergence requires intermediate scales beyond the scope of this study.
50	
51	\subsection{Per-Example Divergence}\label{ssec:per_example}
52	
53	The aggregate convergence on LAMBADA raises a question: do architectures converge by improving on the same examples, or do they help and hurt different examples when attention is added? We compare each architecture's pure-recurrent baseline against its h3-1 hybrid variant on 5{,}153 LAMBADA examples, classifying each example as helped (correct only in hybrid), hurt (correct only in pure), or unchanged.
54	
55	Table~\ref{tab:per_example} reports the results. Each architecture displays a distinct profile of per-example changes. GDN experiences a net loss of 153 examples (462 helped, 615 hurt), RetNet a net loss of 69 (426 helped, 495 hurt), and HGRN2 a net gain of 153 (548 helped, 395 hurt). The directional asymmetry is notable: HGRN2 is the only architecture for which attention produces a net benefit at the per-example level, while GDN and RetNet both lose more examples than they gain. Pairwise Jaccard similarity between any two architectures' affected sets is low: $J \leq 0.104$ for helped sets and $J \leq 0.096$ for hurt sets, both near the chance-level baseline for sets of this size. Each architecture is therefore affected on a largely non-overlapping subset of examples.
56	
57	We tested whether surface-level features (token count, word frequency, syntactic complexity) predict which examples are helped or hurt within a given architecture. No feature reliably separates helped from hurt examples for any single architecture. A cross-architecture analysis, however, reveals structure in the divergence. A Kruskal-Wallis test on the hurt-example distributions across architectures is significant ($p = .0005$), and the corresponding test for helped examples also reaches significance ($p = .020$). The architecture-specific patterns of per-example effects are therefore structured rather than random, even though the source of this structure lies beyond simple surface features. This structured disagreement at the individual-example level, despite similar aggregate performance, connects to the underspecification phenomenon documented by \citet{damour2022underspecification}.
58	
59	\begin{table}[t]
60	\centering
61	\caption{Per-example effects of attention (pure $\to$ h3-1) on 5{,}153 LAMBADA examples at 1.3B scale. $J_{\max}$: maximum pairwise Jaccard similarity with other architectures across helped and hurt sets.}
62	\label{tab:per_example}
63	\begin{tabular}{lrrrr}
64	\toprule
65	Architecture & Helped & Hurt & Net & $J_{\max}$ \\
66	\midrule
67	GDN & 462 & 615 & $-$153 & .096 \\
68	RetNet & 426 & 495 & $-$69 & .100 \\
69	HGRN2 & 548 & 395 & $+$153 & .104 \\
70	\bottomrule
71	\end{tabular}
72	\end{table}
73	
74	\subsection{Decoupling}\label{ssec:decoupling}
75	
76	The central finding of this paper is that aggregate convergence and per-example divergence operate on different timescales as attention ratio increases (Figure~\ref{fig:decoupling}).
77	
78	Cross-architecture $\sigma$ decreases gradually across the five attention ratios: $0.024 \to 0.016 \to 0.014 \to 0.006 \to 0.005$. Each additional attention layer provides incremental reduction. In contrast, pairwise Jaccard similarity between architectures' per-example effects saturates at the first attention level (4\% attention): approximately 0.095 for helped examples, with no further increase at higher ratios. Net asymmetry between architectures' per-example profiles increases from 0.013 at 4\% attention to 0.040 at 25\%.
79	
80	These three quantities follow distinct trajectories. Aggregate variance requires progressively more attention to reduce. Per-example overlap reaches its ceiling with minimal attention. The asymmetry between architectures' per-example profiles grows as attention increases. This separation of timescales constitutes a decoupling: attention reduces the aggregate performance gap but does not homogenize per-example behavior. The per-example divergence in fact increases with attention ratio.
81	
82	An analysis of attention weight patterns provides partial insight into this decoupling. At layer 2 of the 1.3B h3-1 models, GDN and RetNet produce nearly identical attention distributions (cosine similarity 0.995), yet their per-example effects differ substantially. HGRN2 attention patterns diverge from the other architectures at early layers (cosine $\sim$0.20) but converge at deeper layers ($>$0.94 at layer 20). Attention entropy does not differ between helped and hurt examples, which indicates that the per-example effects originate in the recurrent layers rather than in the attention mechanism itself. Full results appear in Appendix~D.
83	
84	\subsection{Robustness}\label{ssec:robustness}
85	
86	We test sensitivity to architecture inclusion by removing GDN and recomputing all correlations. The LAMBADA correlation weakens from $\rho = -1.0$ to $\rho = -0.7$ ($p = .233$), and MMLU reverses direction from $\rho = -0.7$ to $\rho = +0.6$. These shifts confirm that individual architectures influence the aggregate trends, consistent with the per-example divergence reported in \S\ref{ssec:per_example}. The 11.25\% degenerate bootstrap resamples in our BCa analysis arise from same-architecture triplicates that produce undefined $\rho$ (not $\rho = 0$); the percentile CI remains valid with 88.75\% informative resamples. Full sensitivity analyses appear in the appendix.
87

## 任务：撰写论文 Method §3

你需要撰写论文的 Method 部分（§3），输出纯 LaTeX 内容。

## 写作前必读

先 Read 以下两个 skill 文件，严格遵守其中规范：
1. `/home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/paper-writing-norms.skill.md`

## 论文信息

**标题**: "Aggregate Convergence, Per-Example Divergence: Decoupled Effects of Attention in Hybrid Recurrent Architectures"
**投稿目标**: EMNLP 2026 (ARR June cycle), Findings track
**核心 Claim**: Adding attention to hybrid recurrent architectures reduces cross-architecture variance by 79% on LAMBADA, but per-example helped/hurt sets remain nearly disjoint (Jaccard < 0.10) and saturate at minimal attention — aggregate convergence and per-example divergence are decoupled.

## Method §3 Outline（word budget: 750 words，严格控制）

### §3.1 Model Zoo
- Wang et al. (2025) pretrained model zoo: 3 architectures (GatedDeltaNet, RetNet, HGRN2) × 5 attention ratios (0% pure recurrent, 4%, 7.7%, 14.3%, 25%) × 2 scales (340M, 1.3B parameters)
- 命名法：h$k$-1 表示每 $k{+}1$ 层中插入 1 层 attention；h3-1 = 25%, h6-1 = 14.3%, h12-1 = 7.7%, h24-1 = 4%, pure = 0%
- 另含 Transformer baseline（纯 attention）
- 同一 scale 内所有模型共享相同训练数据和超参数，仅架构和 attention 配置不同
- 引用：\citet{wang2025hybrid}

### §3.2 Task Taxonomy（pre-defined, NOT post-hoc）
- 4 个类别（这是 pre-registered 的分类法 D003，不是 post-hoc）：
  - **Retrieval**: LAMBADA — next-token prediction requiring long-range context without reasoning/knowledge
  - **Comprehension**: BoolQ — reading comprehension/QA
  - **Reasoning**: HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, WinoGrande, PIQA, COPA(supplementary, n=100)
  - **Mixed**: ARC-Easy, MMLU, SciQ, XStoryCloze — multiple skills
- 评估框架：lm-evaluation-harness \citep{gao2024lmeval}
- 10 benchmarks in main analysis + COPA supplementary

### §3.3 Convergence Metrics
- 对每个 benchmark，在每个 attention ratio 计算 3 个架构的 cross-architecture standard deviation σ
- Spearman rank correlation ρ：attention ratio rank 与 σ 之间的相关性（n=5 attention ratios）
- Convergence ratio = σ_pure / σ_{h3-1}：> 1 表示 attention 减少了跨架构差异

### §3.4 Per-Example Decomposition
- 比较每个架构的 pure baseline 与 h3-1 hybrid，在 LAMBADA 5,153 个样本上逐样本分类：
  - Helped: hybrid 正确但 pure 错误
  - Hurt: pure 正确但 hybrid 错误
  - Unchanged: 两者一致
- Net effect = |helped| - |hurt|
- 跨架构 pairwise Jaccard J = |A∩B| / |A∪B|：衡量两个架构的 helped/hurt 集合重叠度

### §3.5 Statistical Methods
- Exact permutation test: n=5 attention ratios, 5! = 120 permutations, two-tailed
- BCa bootstrap CI: 10,000 resamples at architecture level; percentile CI when BCa degenerates at boundary
- Bonferroni correction: 6 pre-registered benchmarks (D003); 剩余 4 benchmarks 报 10-benchmark Bonferroni
- Mann-Whitney U: within-architecture comparisons (helped vs hurt sample properties)
- Kruskal-Wallis: cross-architecture comparisons of per-example effect distributions

## 叙事约束（硬规则）

- 禁用词：paradox, paradoxical, co-evolution, co-evolve, mechanistic analysis, remarkably, extensive experiments demonstrate
- 禁止破折号（em-dash —, 解释性 en-dash –）
- 禁止 -ing 短语结尾（如 "..., highlighting the..."）
- 禁止连续 Furthermore/Moreover/Additionally
- 不说 "significantly" 除非有统计检验
- 不说 "state-of-the-art"（没有 SOTA 比较）
- 不说 "consistently outperforms"（单 benchmark）
- Method 是描述性章节，不要提前剧透实验结果（结果在 §4）

## Notation 约定（全文统一）

- σ: cross-architecture standard deviation
- ρ: Spearman rank correlation
- J: pairwise Jaccard similarity
- h-k-1: hybrid with 1 attention layer per k+1 total layers (e.g., h3-1 = 25% attention)

\section{Experiments}\label{sec:experiments}

We analyze how attention affects cross-architecture performance variance using models from the hybrid recurrent model zoo of \citet{wang2025hybrid}. Our analysis spans three architectures (GatedDeltaNet, RetNet, HGRN2), five attention ratios (0\% pure recurrent, 4\%, 7.7\%, 14.3\%, 25\%), and two scales (340M and 1.3B parameters). In the h$k$-1 notation used throughout, one attention layer is interleaved per every $k{+}1$ layers; h3-1 denotes 25\% attention. All models within each scale share identical training data and hyperparameters; they differ only in architecture and attention configuration. We evaluate on 10 benchmarks spanning retrieval, comprehension, reasoning, and mixed task categories, plus one supplementary benchmark (COPA, $n = 100$).
